text.S1: Once upon a time there were four little Rabbits, and their names were— Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter.
text.S2: A long time ago, there were four little Rabbits, and their names were— Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter.
text.T1: Kalekale panali a kalulu anai ang’onoang’ono, ndipo maina awo anali Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton tail ndi Peter.
text.T2: Kalekale panali a kalulu anai ang’onoang’ono, ndipo maina awo anali Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton tail ndi Peter.

text.S1: They lived with their Mother in a sand-bank, underneath the root of a very big fir-tree.
text.S2: They lived with their Mother in a sand-bank, underneath the root of a very big fir-tree.
text.T1: Amakhala ndi amai awo mphepete mwa mchenga, m’munsi mwa muzyu wa mtengo waukulu waubweya.
text.T2: Amakhala ndi amai awo mumulu wa mchenga, m’munsi mwa muzyu wa mtengo waukulu waubweya.

text.S1: 'Now my dears,' said old Mrs. Rabbit one morning, 'you may go into the fields or down the lane, but don't go into Mr. McGregor's garden: your Father had an accident there; he was put in a pie by Mrs. McGregor.'
text.S2: 'Now my dears,' said old Mrs. Rabbit one morning, 'you may go into the fields or down the lane, but don't go into Mr. McGregor's garden: your Father had an accident there; he was eatene by Mrs. McGregor.'
text.T1: ‘Tsopano inu okondedwa’, anatero amai achikulire a Mrs Rabbit m’mawa,’ mungathe kupita m’minda kapena m’mphepete, koma osapita mdimba la a McGreory; atate anu anapezeka mngozi kumene kuja; anadyedwa nyama ndi a Mrs. McGregor.
text.T2: ‘Tsopano inu okondedwa’, anatero amai achikulire a Mrs Rabbit m’mawa,’ mungapite m’minda kapena m’mphepete, koma osapita mdimba la a McGreory; atate anu anapezeka mngozi kumene kuja; anadyedwa ndi a Mrs. McGregor.

text.S1: 'Now run along, and don't get into mischief. I am going out.'
text.S2: 'Now run along, and don't get into mischief. I am going out.'
text.T1: ’Tsopano thamangani, ndipo osazigwetsa m’mabvuto.
text.T2: ’Tsopano thamangani, ndipo osapezeka mubvuto.

text.S1: Then old Mrs. Rabbit took a basket and her umbrella, and went through the wood to the baker's. She bought a loaf of brown bread and five currant buns.
text.S2: Then old Mrs. Rabbit took a basket and her umbrella, and went through the bush to the baker's. She bought a loaf of brown bread and five currant buns.
text.T1: Ndipo mzimai wachikulire ananyamula swanda ndi ambulela, anapita mthengo kupita komwe apangira zinkhwa. Anakagula cinkhwa ca mgaiwa ndi mabanzi a tizipatso ta vinyo.
text.T2: Ndipo mzimai wachikulire amai Rabbit ananyamula swanda ndi ambulela, anapita mthengo kupita komwe amapangira zinkhwa. Anakagula cinkhwa ca mgaiwa ndi mabanzi a tizipatso ta vinyo.

text.S1: Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail, who were good little bunnies, went down the lane to gather blackberries:
text.S2: Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail, who were good little bunnies, went to gather blackberries:
text.T1: Flopsy,Mopsy ndi Cotton tail, amene anali akalulu owoneka bwino, anapita kukatola zipatso;
text.T2: Flopsy,Mopsy ndi Cotton tail, amene anali akalulu owoneka bwino, anapita kukatola zipatso;

text.S1: But Peter, who was very naughty, ran straight away to Mr. McGregor's garden, and squeezed under the gate!
text.S2: But Peter, who was very naughty, ran straight away to Mr. McGregor's garden, and squeezed under the gate!
text.T1: Koma Peter yemwe anali wosamvera, anathamangira mdimba la a McGregor, nazipapatiza polowerera.
text.T2: Koma Peter yemwe anali wosamvera, anathamangira mdimba la a McGregor, nazipapatiza polowerera.

text.S1: First he ate some lettuces and some French beans; and then he ate some radishes;
text.S2: First he ate some lettuces and some French beans; and then he ate some roots;
text.T1: Poyamba anadya ndiwo zamasamba za letisi ndi kayera wa ku France. Ndiposno anadya mizyu.
text.T2: Poyamba anadya ndiwo zamasamba za letisi ndi kayera wa ku France.

text.S1: And then, feeling rather sick, he went to look for some parsley.
text.S2: And then, feeling rather sick, he went to look for some parsley.
text.T1: Ndipo, pakumva kudwalira, anapita kukafuna mayani ya pasile.
text.T2: Ndipo, pakumva kudwalira, anapita kukafuna mayani ya pasile

text.S1: But round the end of a cucumber frame, whom should he meet but Mr. McGregor!
text.S2: But round the end of a cucumber frame, whom should he meet but Mr. McGregor!
text.T1: Koma pothera kwa fulemu yamnkhaka, kodi angawonane ndi yani koma a Mr McGregor!
text.T2: Koma pothera kwa fulemu yamnkhaka, kodi angawonane ndi yani koma a Mr McGregor!

text.S1: Mr. McGregor was on his hands and knees planting out young cabbages, but he jumped up and ran after Peter, waving a rake and calling out, 'Stop thief!'
text.S2: Mr. McGregor was on his hands and knees planting out young cabbages, but he jumped up and ran after Peter, waving a rake and screaming, 'thief!'
text.T1: A McGregor anali pamanja ndi maondo kubyala kabichi, koma analumpha ndi kuthamingira Peter, ali ndi ndi leki m’manja akuweyula ali kukuwa kuti,’ kawalala’
text.T2: A McGregor anali pamanja ndi maondo kubyala kabichi, koma analumpha ndi kuthamingira Peter, ali ndi ndi leki m’manja akuweyula ali kukuwa kuti,’ kawalala’

text.S1: Peter was most dreadfully frightened; he rushed all over the garden, for he had forgotten the way back to the gate. He lost one of his shoes among the cabbages, and the other shoe amongst the potatoes.
text.S2: Peter was gripped with fear; he ran round the garden, for he had forgotten the way out. He lost one of his shoes among the cabbages, and the other shoe amongst the potatoes.
text.T1: Peter anagwidwa ndi mantha kwambiri; anayamba kuzungulira mdimba mofulumira, cifukwa anasowa njira yotulukirako. Anataya nsapato imodzi ku makabichi, ndipo inanso ku mbatatisi.
text.T2: Peter anagwidwa ndi mantha kwambiri; anayamba kuzungulira mdimba mofulumira, cifukwa anaiwala njira yotulukirako. Anataya nsapato imodzi ku makabichi, ndipo inanso ku mbatatisi

text.S1: After losing them, he ran on four legs and went faster, so that I think he might have got away altogether if he had not unfortunately run into a gooseberry net, and got caught by the large buttons on his jacket. It was a blue jacket with brass buttons, quite new.
text.S2: After losing them, he ran on four legs and went faster, so that I think he might have got away altogether if he had not unfortunately run into a gooseberry net, and got caught by the large buttons on his jacket. It was a blue jacket with brass buttons, quite new.
text.T1: Atasowedwa, anathamanga pamiyendo anai ndipo mwamsangamsanga, m’maganizo yanga anakakwaniritsa kuzemba ngati mwatsoka lanji sanagwidwe muukonde, anagwidwa cifukwa ca mabatani akuluakulu a jekete lake. Inali jekete lobiriwirira ndi mabatani owoneka ngati mkuwa, ndipo anali a tsopano.
text.T2: Atasowedwa, anathamanga pamiyendo anai ndipo mwamsangamsanga, m’maganizo yanga anakakwaniritsa kuzemba ngati mwatsoka lanji sanagwidwe muukonde, anagwidwa cifukwa ca mabatani akuluakulu a jekete lake. Inali jekete lobiriwirira ndi mabatani owoneka ngati mkuwa, ndipo anali a tsopano.

text.S1: Peter gave himself up for lost, and shed big tears; but his sobs were overheard by some friendly sparrows, who flew to him in great excitement, and implored him to exert himself.
text.S2: Peter gave himself up for lost, and shed big tears; but his sobs were overheard by some friendly sparrows, who flew to him in great excitement, and implored him to exert himself.
text.T1: Peter andzipereka kwa kusoweka, anagwetsa misozi yaikuluikulu; koma kulira kwake kunamveka kwa machacha aubwenzi, amene anauluka kwa iye mokondwa kwambiri, ndi kumulimbitsa kuti alimbike.
text.T2: Peter andzipereka kwa kusoweka, anagwetsa misozi yaikuluikulu; koma kulira kwake kunamveka kwa machacha aubwenzi, amene anauluka kwa iye mokondwa kwambiri, ndi kumulimbitsa kuti alimbike.

text.S1: Mr. McGregor came up with a sieve, which he intended to pop upon the top of Peter; but Peter wriggled out just in time, leaving his jacket behind him.
text.S2: Mr. McGregor came up with a sieve, which he intended to cover Peter with; but Peter wriggled out just in time, leaving his jacket behind him.
text.T1: A McGregor anabweretsa sefa, yomwe anafuna kuvundikira Peter; koma Peter analewa msanga, kusiya jekete lake kumbuyo.
text.T2: A McGregor anabweretsa sefa, yomwe anafuna kuvundikira Peter; koma Peter analewa msanga, kusiya jekete lake kumbuyo.

text.S1: And rushed into the tool-shed, and jumped into a can. It would have been a beautiful thing to hide in, if it had not had so much water in it.
text.S2: And rushed into the tool-shed, and jumped into a can. It would have been a beautiful thing to hide in, if it had not had so much water in it.
text.T1: Anafulumira kupita ku nyumba yosungiramo zitsulo, ndipo analumphira muchibekete. Cinakakhala cinthu cabwino kubisalamo, kuti kunalibe madzi ya mbiri mkatimo.
text.T2: Anafulumira kupita ku nyumba yosungiramo zitsulo, ndipo analumphira muchibekete. Cinakakhala cinthu cabwino kubisalamo, kuti kunalibe madzi ya mbiri mkatimo.

text.S1: Mr. McGregor was quite sure that Peter was somewhere in the tool-shed, perhaps hidden underneath a flower-pot. He began to turn them over carefully, looking under each. Presently Peter sneezed—'Kertyschoo!' Mr. McGregor was after him in no time.
text.S2: Mr. McGregor was quite sure that Peter was where tools are kept, perhaps hidden underneath a flower-pot. He began to turn them over carefully, looking under each. Presently Peter sneezed—'Kertyschoo!' Mr. McGregor followed him in no time.
text.T1: A McGregor anali ndi cikhulupiliro kuti Peter mwina mwache ali mosungira zitsulo, mwina kunsi kwa poto wa maluwa. Anayamba kusanankhula mbali yonse kupenyapenya munsi mwa ma poto onse. Pomwepo Peter anayetsemula –“ Yetsee!” Abambo McGregor anamlondola mosataya nthawi.
text.T2: A McGregor anali ndi cikhulupiliro kuti Peter mwina mwache ali mosungira zitsulo, mwina kunsi kwa poto wa maluwa. Anayamba kusanankhula mbali yonse kupenyapenya munsi mwa ma poto onse. Pomwepo Peter anayetsemula –“ Yetsee!” Abambo McGregor anamlondola mosataya nthawi.

text.S1: And tried to put his foot upon Peter, who jumped out of a window, upsetting three plants. The window was too small for Mr. McGregor, and he was tired of running after Peter. He went back to his work.
text.S2: And step on Peter with his leg, who jumped out of a window, upsetting three plants. The window was too small for Mr. McGregor, and he was tired of running after Peter. He went back to his work.
text.T1: Anayesa kuponda Peter ndi mwendo, amene analumphila pa dzenera, kugudubula zomera zitatu.Dzenera linali laling’ono kwa Abambo McGregor, ndipo analema kuthamangitsa Peter. Anabwelera kunchito yawo.
text.T2: Anayesa kuponda Peter ndi mwendo, amene analumphila pa dzenera, kugudubula zomera zitatu.Dzenera linali laling’ono kwa Abambo McGregor, ndipo analema kuthamangitsa Peter. Anabwelera kunchito yawo.

text.S1: Peter sat down to rest; he was out of breath and trembling with fright, and he had not the least idea which way to go. Also he was very damp with sitting in that can. After a time he began to wander about, going lippity—lippity—not very fast, and looking all round.
text.S2: Peter sat down to rest; he was failing to breath well and was trembling with fright, and he had not the least idea which way to go. Also he was very damp with sitting in that can. After a time he began to wander about, going lippity—lippity—not very fast, and looking all round.
text.T1: Peter anakhala pansi kupumula; analephera kupuma bwino ndipo ananjenjemera ndi mantha, ndipo analibe ganizo lakuti adzapita kuti. Ndipo anakamuka madzi cifukwa cokhala mu mcibekete cothilira mbeu. Patapita nthawi anayamba kuyendayenda pang’onopang’ono lipiti -lipiti akuyang’anayang’ana.
text.T2: Peter anakhala pansi kupumula; analephera kupuma bwino ndipo ananjenjemera ndi mantha, ndipo analibe ganizo lakuti adzapita kuti. Ndipo anakamuka madzi cifukwa cokhala mu mcibekete cothilira mbeu. Patapita nthawi anayamba kuyendayenda pang’onopang’ono lipiti -lipiti akuyang’anayang’ana.

text.S1: He found a door in a wall; but it was locked, and there was no room for a fat little rabbit to squeeze underneath. An old mouse was running in and out over the stone doorstep, carrying peas and beans to her family in the wood. Peter asked her the way to the gate, but she had such a large pea in her mouth that she could not answer. She only shook her head at him. Peter began to cry.
text.S2: He found a door in a wall; but it was locked, and there was no room for a fat little rabbit to squeeze underneath. text.T1: Anawona citseko mcipupa; koma cinali cotseka, ndipo kunalibe mpata wa kalulu wamng’ono wonenepa kuti kadziphatikize munsi. Khoswe wokalamba ankathamanga polowa ndi kutuluka podutsa pakhomo lamwala, ali kunyamula nyemba ndi kayera kuli banja lake kuthengo. Peter anafunsa njira yotulukira, koma ananyamula nyemba yaikulu mkamwa mwake kotero kuti analephera kuyankha. Adangogwedeza mutu kwa iye. Peter anayamba kulira.
text.T2: Anawona citseko mcipupa; koma cinali cotseka, ndipo kunalibe mpata wa kalulu wamng’ono wonenepa kuti kadziphatikize munsi. text.S1: Then he tried to find his way straight across the garden, but he became more and more puzzled. Presently, he came to a pond where Mr. McGregor filled his water-cans. A white cat was staring at some gold-fish. She sat very, very still, but now and then the tip of her tail twitched as if it were alive. Peter thought it best to go away without speaking to her; he had heard about cats from his cousin, little Benjamin Bunny.
text.S2: Then he tried to find his way straight across the garden, but he became more and more puzzled. Presently, he came to a pond where Mr. McGregor filled his water-cans. text.T1: Anayesa kupeza njira yodutsira mdimba, koma anakhala anasokonezeka kopitilira. Tsopano, anabwera pa dziwe pomwe a McGregor anali kudzadza zibekete ndi madzi. Chona woyera anali kuyang’ana nsomba ya golide. Anakhala mosatekeseka ndipo nsonga lamchila wake uli kubvinabvina monga kuti uli ndi moyo. Peter anaganiza kuti ncaphindu kuti angosamuka popanda kumlankhuza; anamvako za achona kwa msuweni wake Benjamin Bunny.

text.S1: He went back towards the tool-shed, but suddenly, quite close to him, he heard the noise of a hoe—scr-r-ritch, scratch, scratch, scritch. Peter scuttered underneath the bushes. But presently, as nothing happened, he came out, and climbed upon a wheelbarrow and peeped over. The first thing he saw was Mr. McGregor hoeing onions. His back was turned towards Peter, and beyond him was the gate!

text.T1: Anabwerera m’mbuyo kupita kumalo wosungirako zitsulo, koma mwadzidzi, pafupi naiye, ananvera phokoso la khasu kuti ba, ba,ba ba, ndipo Peter anabisala munsi mwazitsamba. Koma posacedwa, monga palibe cacitika, anasokoloka,nakwera wilibara nasonjola. Cinthu coyamba anawona ndi abambo McGregor akulimilira anyenzi. Msana wao uli kumbali yomwe Peter analili, ndipo patsogolo panali potulukira.
text.T2: Anabwerera m’mbuyo kupita kumalo wosungirako zitsulo, koma mwadzidzi, pafupi naiye, ananvera phokoso la khasu kuti ba, ba,ba ba, ndipo Peter anabisala munsi mwazitsamba. Msana wao uli kumbali yomwe Peter analili, ndipo patsogolo panali potulukira.

text.S1: Peter got down very quietly off the wheelbarrow; and started run- ning as fast as he could go, along a straight walk behind some black- currant bushes. Mr. McGregor caught sight of him at the corner, but Peter did not care. He slipped underneath the gate, and was safe at last in the wood outside the garden.
text.S2: Peter got down very quietly off the wheelbarrow; and started run- ning as fast as he could go, along a straight walk behind some black- currant bushes. Mr. McGregor caught sight of him at an angle, but Peter did not care. He slipped underneath the gate, and was safe at last in the wood outside the garden.
text.T1: Peter anatsika mwakacecete pa wilibara; nayamba kuthamanga mwaliwiro wa mtondo wadowoka, molunjika koma kumbuyo kwa tzitsamba zazipatso .A McGrgor anamuwona pangodya, koma Peter sanalabadile. Analowa munsi mwapolowera, ndipo anali wochingirizidwa m’mitengo kubwalo kwa dimba.

text.S1: Mr. McGregor hung up the little jacket and the shoes for a scare-crow to frighten the blackbirds.
text.S2: Mr. McGregor hung up the little jacket and the shoes for a scare-crow to frighten the blackbirds.

text.T2: A McGregor ayedzeka jekete lawo laling’ono ndi nsapato monga kamtande pofuna kuwopyseza mbalame zakuda.

text.S1: Peter never stopped running or looked behind him till he got home to the big fir-tree.
text.S2: Peter never stopped running or looked behind him till he got home to the big fir-tree.

text.T2: Peter sanalekeze kuthamanga kapena kupenya kumbuyo mpaka anafika kunyumba kumtengo wabweya.

text.S1: He was so tired that he flopped down upon the nice soft sand on the floor of the rabbit-hole and shut his eyes. His mother was busy cooking; she wondered what he had done with his clothes. It was the second little jacket and pair of shoes that Peter had lost in a fort-night!

text.S1: I am sorry to say that Peter was not very well during the evening.
text.S2: I am sorry to say that Peter was not very well during the evening.

text.T2: Pepani ponena kuti Peter sanali bwino nthawi yamadzulo.

text.S1: His mother put him to bed, and made some camomile tea; and she gave a dose of it to Peter! 'One table-spoonful to be taken at bed-time.'
text.S2: His mother put him to bed, and made some camomile tea; and she gave a dose of it to Peter! 'One table-spoonful to be taken at bed-time.'

text.T2: Amai ake anamuyika pa bedi, ndi kumpangira mtentha ndebvu wa camomile; ndipo anapatsa Peter.’Sipuni yodzala yaikulu pa nthawi yokagona.

text.S1: But Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail had bread and milk and blackberries for supper.
text.S2: But Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail had bread and milk and fruits for supper.
